sentences.text:
1. The revision petitioners/A1, A2 and A4 were convicted for the offence under Sections 170 and 474 r/w.34 of the Indian Penal Code along with A3 by the Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class,
Bhongir, and sentenced to pay a fine of Rs.1,500/- each for the offence under Section 170 of IPC.

entities.text:
Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class,
Bhongir
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
A1,
A2 and A4 were sentenced to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for a period of six months and also to pay a fine of Rs.1,500/- each and A3 is sentenced to pay fine of Rs.1,500/- for the offence under Section 474 r/w.34 of the IPC.
Aggrieved by the same, A1, A2 & A4 preferred appeal.
. Since A3 was sentenced to fine only, no appeal was preferred.
The learned Sessions Judge confirmed the conviction and sentence imposed by the trial Court.
Questioning the said order of the learned Sessions Judge, petitioners are before this Court.

2. Heard learned counsel for the revision petitioners and learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for the respondent-State.
3.

The case of the prosecution is that on 17.09.2005, when PW3 who is the Inspector along with his driver-PW1, Police Constable-PW2, went to Bhongir for 'Bandobast' duty and while returning around 4.00 a.m. accused No.3 stopped their jeep and asked PW1-driver to produce the documents of the vehicle stating that Motor Vehicle Inspector is sitting in the Indica Car, on which PW3-Inspector got down from the jeep and enquired A1, who was sitting in the Car.
A2 and A4 were standing outside the car who tried to flee, however, they were apprehended.
PW3-Inspector then interrogated A1 and thereafter complaint was filed which is Ex.P1.
After investigation, the Police filed charge sheet for the offence under Sections 171, 172, 384, 420, 465, 466, 468 and 474 r/w.34 of the Indian Penal Code.

4. PWs.1, 2 and 3 who are Police Personnel stated before Court below that the accused have impersonated as Motor Vehicle Inspector and were also in possession of Vehicle Check Report which would be maintained by the Transport Department.
5. Learned trial Judge found favour with the evidence of PWs.1 to 3 and accordingly convicted the accused.
6. Learned Sessions Judge in appeal confirmed conviction recorded by the Court below.
7. Learned Counsel appearing for the revision petitioners would submit that PWs.4 to 6 are independent witnesses and apart from PWs.1 to 3, no other witnesses have stated against these accused.

sentences.text: The identification badges seized from the accused were also not produced before the Court.
In the said circumstances, conviction has to be set aside.
8. PWs.1 to 3 who are Police officials were stopped by the accused impersonating themselves as Motor Vehicle Inspectors.
When the accused found that the persons whom they have stopped were police officials tried to run away, however, they were caught.
No reasons are given as to why the accused would be implicated in a police case by PWs.1 to 3 who are strangers.
There are no grounds to interfere with the conviction recorded by the Court below.

However, since the case is of the year 2005 and 19 years have passed by and further on instructions learned Assistant Public Prosecutor submits that there are no other cases pending against these petitioners, this Court deems it appropriate to reduce the sentence of imprisonment of the petitioners to the period already undergone by them.
9. Accordingly, Criminal Revision Case is partly allowed.
As a sequel, miscellaneous applications, if any, pending shall stand closed.
